description: Open a crypto page — a dApp, airdrop, claim or mint link — and report what it asks a wallet to do. DechoNet opens it in an isolated Chromium (Seoul) with a test wallet that holds nothing (EVM and Solana): it presses the page's "Connect wallet" button once (or one "Claim" button when there is none) and the test wallet in a wallet picker once; it types nothing and submits no form, and the test wallet connects with a burn address and refuses every signature and transaction. Reported: each wallet request in order with what approving it would allow (unlimited token approvals, setApprovalForAll, Permit/Permit2 signatures, transfers, Solana transactions), drainer-kit code markers in the page scripts, a connect button that sends the visitor to another site, and the phishing link check verdict of the same link (including whether it is the brand's own domain). Verdicts: danger, suspicious, official, no_signals, unreachable. no_signals means none of these were seen and is not a statement that the page is harmless: drainers that wait for a second press, show nothing to an automated browser or ask only after a sign-in can go unseen, and on new drainer samples few were caught by wallet requests alone (figures on dechonet.com/methodology); 'unchecked' lists what was not looked at. Every call opens the page (no cached answer), so it takes longer than the other checks, and it has a per-minute rate limit and a daily limit shared by all callers. Only the host, the verdict and the kinds of request are kept (90 days); no API key.
